key_insight: Adaptive, resource-aware batch Bayesian optimization can better balance exploration and exploitation in autonomous materials discovery, improving Pareto-front learning under changing campaign constraints.
engineering_relevance: For self-driving laboratories, the work suggests that dynamically reallocating experiments can reduce uncertainty and preserve discovery efficiency when budgets, timelines, or other resources shift.
method: Compared three allocation policies: exploitation-focused, fixed mixed exploratory/exploitative, and LLM-based adaptive strategies.
Tested multi-objective Bayesian optimization on two materials systems: a septenary refractory high-entropy alloy and an Fe-Co-Ni soft magnetic alloy.
Evaluated performance under baseline and mid-campaign disruptions including budget cuts, timeline reductions, and combined resource events.
evidence_signal: Across the abstracted benchmarks, mixed and adaptive allocation strategies gained substantially more mutual information than pure exploitation, with adaptive policies improving over fixed-mixed allocation under resource disruptions.
watch_item: Results are benchmark-based, so real-world gains may depend on the quality of the campaign state signals and the reliability of the LLM-driven allocation decisions.
paper_title: Agentic Resource Allocation for Batch Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization in Autonomous Materials Discovery
